Line numbers are read off the fixture's own text: 14 `<Panel>`, 15 `<Widget />`, 16 `<Ns.Chart />`, 19 the nested `<Widget />`. `expectExactly` is an extension consumed by script/m14/ts-renders-probe.ts (the shared fixture runner ignores an unknown key), because 'ONE row for the paired element' is an exact-count claim that `expectRelationships` (>=1) structurally cannot make.
rationale: PINS the `renders` relabel (vocabulary extension, 2026-10-18). The expected rows were `uses{jsxElement}` before it — a label claiming the app's source MENTIONS the component rather than that it RENDERS it. Forbid rows guard the three shapes the rule is easy to over-apply to: a lowercase intrinsic tag (`<div>`, `<section>`) is not a component, a fragment is not a component, and `React.createElement(Widget, null)` is a call of `createElement` whose first ARGUMENT is a component — if that ever fires as `renders`, the CSS/test corpus would gain a fabricated rendering edge for every imperative createElement. `expectExactly` pins the one-row-per-element rule, which is the difference between reading the element and reading its opening tag. MEASURED BOUND OF THE NAME RULE, recorded rather than expanded (the relabel is 1:1 by the owner's direction): a QUALIFIED component `<Ns.Chart />` writes a `member_expression` tag in tree-sitter-tsx (measured on this grammar: jsx_self_closing_element > member_expression), while the current branch matches `identifier` and `nested_identifier`; so a qualified component emits NO renders row today. That is the pre-existing name rule, not a regression of the relabel, and widening it would change the emitted-count 1:1 property, so it is left as a measured gap with its own decision rather than folded in here. `Ns.Chart` stays in the fixture source for that reason, with no expected row.
